newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tractebel in talks for Kazakh gas network.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel in talks for Kazakh gas network.

text.p: Kazakhstan has invited Belgium's Tractebel to negotiate for the right to manage the country's natural gas pipeline network after talks with Argentina's Bridas Energy Corp were deadlocked, an official said on Thursday.

"After Bridas was deprived of the right to lead exclusive negotiations (with the government), we decided to hold separate talks with each company," Sarybay Kalmyrzayev, head of the finance ministry's state property department, told reporters late on Thursday. "We are now negotiating with Tractebel."
Earlier this year, Bridas defeated a consortium comprising U.S. company Enron Corp and Gaz de France in a tender to negotiate a contract to manage Kazakhstan's gas pipeline network for 15 years.
But the government complained that after Bridas was announced the winner, it offered less than it had initially.

"When we got to working out a contract, they (Bridas) started speculating, offering royalties of 0.9 percent (of the cost of gas transported in Kazakhstan's pipeline network), while the initial offer in the tender was 3.0 perecnt," Kalmyrzayev said.
Enron and Gaz de France, which offered royalties of 1.42 percent, lost in the tender against Bridas.
Kalmyrzayev said that Tractebel has offered royalties of 1.5 percent but stressed that Bridas and the Enron/Gaz de France alliance were still welcome to negotiate with the government.

He said the offer of Bridas and Tractebel to manage both the Batystransgas pipeline network in western Kazakhstan, which also transports Turkmen gas to Russia and Europe, and the Alaugaz company in the south, which distributes gas mainly to local consumers, were very advantageous for the government.
"The main condition is that royalties should not be lower than those offered by Enron and Gaz de France," Kalmyrzayev said.
Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said earlier this month that Gaz de France and Enron were only interested in the western pipeline network.

Tractebel already supplies the Kazakh capital Almaty with thermal power and electricity. The company bought several power stations in the Almaty region for $250 million in August last year and pledged to invest another $340 million over the next 10 years.
